name: Resources
blurb: Every AWS resource this repository creates, what configures it, and which stack owns it.
audience: Cost, audit and incident scoping — and the detail behind every badge
note: Counts follow the stage selector in the header. They differ because domains, routes and whole stacks are gated by their environments array — and because an ephemeral PR stage reuses the development core rather than building its own. Entries whose meta reads varies carry no number, so any group total that includes one is a floor rather than a total.

d.role: One per persistent environment.
facts: Availability zones are pinned to eu-west-2a/b/c rather than looked up.
An ephemeral PR stage creates none — it imports the development VPC through addExternalExports.

d.role: Carry the NAT gateways. No workloads.
facts: 251 usable addresses each.

d.role: Home of every access: private Lambda.
facts: 8,187 usable addresses each.
Default route goes to the NAT gateway in the same AZ.

d.role: Home of every access: isolated Lambda — the default tier.
facts: No route to a NAT gateway or the internet gateway.

d.role: One per AZ, so losing an AZ does not remove egress for the others.
facts: The single most expensive always-on resource in the network.

d.role: One per NAT gateway.
facts: These are the source addresses DVLA sees.

d.role: The only door to the internet.
facts: Reachable from the public subnets only.

d.role: One per subnet, plus the default association.
facts: exportVpc publishes the nine route table IDs as three comma-joined SSM parameters — public, private and isolated — so another stack can reconstruct the VPC.
The isolated tier's tables carry only the local route.

d.role: Stateless filtering on the public tier.
facts: Rules 80 VPC loopback, 90–92 deny system ports and RDP, 200/210 ephemeral return, 32000 allow outbound.
Rule 80 is evaluated before the denies, so VPC-internal traffic is allowed first and the 90–92 denies only ever apply to traffic from outside the VPC.

d.role: Same rule set as the public tier.
facts: Identical to the public NACL — the difference between the tiers is routing, not filtering.

d.role: The strictest of the three.
facts: Has the VPC loopback pair and the 90–92 denies, but no ephemeral-return and no outbound-allow rule — outbound is permitted only to the VPC CIDR by rule 80.
That omission is what forces isolated Lambdas through the interface endpoints, which sit inside the VPC CIDR.

d.role: Attached to every access: private function.
facts: No explicit rules are needed or added.

d.role: Attached to every access: isolated function.
facts: Gains one egress rule per interface endpoint, TCP 443 to that endpoint's security group.
Adding an endpoint opens the path automatically; nothing else does.

d.role: Receive the isolated tier's egress rules.
facts: Every endpoint SG already allows 443 from the VPC CIDR — addInterfaceEndpoint defaults open to true.
The KMS endpoint additionally gets an explicit ingress rule per isolated subnet CIDR, the one endpoint addressed by range rather than by group.

d.role: API Gateway, CloudWatch Logs, Secrets Manager, SSM, STS, KMS.
facts: The API Gateway endpoint ID is exported as /{env}/flex/vpc-e/api-gateway and pinned in the private API's resource policy.
No gateway endpoints (S3, DynamoDB) exist — nothing needs them.
There is no cognito-idp endpoint, which is why the authorizer sits in the egress tier.

d.role: Full-fidelity network records to S3.
facts: Extended beyond ALL_DEFAULT_FIELDS with VPC ID, subnet ID, instance ID, TCP flags, packet source and destination addresses, and flow direction.

d.role: 7 public routes and 1 private route, one function each.
facts: The only domain whose common.access is private, so its functions sit in the egress subnets and can reach NAT.
Deploys to development, staging and production — plus every ephemeral PR and personal stage.

d.tech: NODEJS_24_X · 20s default (one route at 25s) · isolated access
d.role: 6 public routes and 2 private routes.
facts: Owns the private GET /v1/users/push-id route that uns, groups and example all depend on.

d.role: 4 public notification routes.
facts: Every route pairs a uns gateway call with a udp push-ID lookup.

d.role: GET and POST /v1/groups.
facts: environments is development and staging only — so nothing reaches production, but every ephemeral PR and personal stage still gets both.

d.role: Two private routes only.
facts: The one domain with no public routes, so its stack creates no TokenAuthorizer.
Development and staging, plus every ephemeral PR and personal stage.

d.tech: NODEJS_24_X · 20s default (one route at 30s) · isolated access
d.role: 11 public and 2 private reference routes.
facts: The development environment only — which means every ephemeral PR and personal stage gets it too, and staging and production never do.
Exercises feature flags, all four resource types and both integration kinds, including one that calls its own private route.

d.role: GET /v1/countries and GET /v1/events.
facts: environments is development and staging only, so nothing reaches production — but every ephemeral PR and personal stage still gets both.
Both routes reach the travel service gateway over the private API; the domain itself holds no credentials.

d.role: Sole holder of DVLA credentials.
facts: Mounted at ANY /gateways/dvla/{proxy+} — the ten routes are matched in code, not by API Gateway.
Runs in the egress tier because DVLA is a public-internet API reached through NAT.
Caches the upstream JWKS in a module-level variable across warm invocations.

d.role: Sole holder of UDP credentials.
facts: SigV4 with credentials from sts:AssumeRole, optionally carrying an ExternalId, plus an x-api-key header.

No internet route — isolated subnets, no NAT. Reachability of the UDP endpoint depends on consumerConfig.apiUrl resolving through the API Gateway interface endpoint; unlike uns, the udp gateway schema has no privateApiUrl field at all.

d.role: Sole holder of UNS credentials.
facts: Targets consumerConfig.privateApiUrl with a SigV4-signed assumed role, plus an X-API-KEY header.

d.role: Sole holder of the travel upstream credentials.
facts: Mounted at ANY /gateways/travel/{proxy+} — its two routes are matched in code, not by API Gateway.
environments is development and staging only, so it does not exist in production.
code: the routes, access tier and environments

d.role: API Gateway TOKEN authorizer.
facts: Env: USERPOOL_ID, CLIENT_ID, JWKS_URI (plus AWS_REGION) — Zod-parsed on every invocation, since the verifier is constructed inside the handler rather than at module scope.
One function shared by every domain stack via an SSM-exported ARN.
Sits in the egress tier so it can fetch the Cognito JWKS over NAT — there is no cognito-idp VPC endpoint.

d.role: Serves a JWKS so E2E tests can self-sign tokens.
facts: Publicly reachable by design, with a recorded CKV_AWS_258 suppression.
Exists wherever env resolves to development — so ephemeral PR and personal stages get one too.
A plain NodejsFunction: no VPC, no X-Ray, no explicit log group and no alarms.

d.role: Synthetic canary against the public URL — and, in production, the second caller of the public path after the app itself.
facts: Calls https://{host}/app/udp/v1/users/me with a real access token and, where configured, an X-Firebase-App-Check header, then publishes Flex/SmokeTest.SmokeTestSuccess as 1 or 0.
Hand-written execution role rather than a generated one; the only role in the app with an explicit physical name.
Default Lambda alarms are switched off — the canary is itself the health signal.
Persistent environments only; ephemeral and personal stages get none.

d.role: Republish a us-east-1 SNS message onto the eu-west-2 alarm topic — currently non-functional.
facts: The inline handler interpolates TopicArn: ${targetTopicArn}, without quotes, so the deployed source is a JavaScript syntax error and the function fails at module load on every invocation. Cross-region alarms do not reach Slack today.
One per severity, because CloudWatch cannot target a cross-region topic.
Passes through message and message attributes; truncates the subject to 100 characters.
No explicit log group and no alarms — these are plain Function constructs, not Flex ones.

d.role: Backing functions for custom resources. Deploy machinery, not request path.
facts: An AwsCustomResource singleton per stack, used for cross-region SSM reads and the two API deployments. The Macie stack would add three more, but its import and its instantiation are both commented out in app.ts — it is disabled in code, not merely undeployed.
CfnPause adds an inline timeout function plus a Provider framework function.
BucketDeployment adds an asset-copying handler that also invalidates CloudFront.

d.role: Correlation ID and structural JWT validation at the edge.
facts: Built with esbuild targeting ES5 plus an explicit JS 2.0 feature allow-list.
The construct throws at synth if the handler is an arrow function rather than a declaration.

d.role: Rewrites /docs and /docs/ to the Swagger UI index.
facts: /docs redirects 301 to /docs/, which rewrites to /docs/index.html.

d.role: The app-facing surface.
facts: endpointAccessMode BASIC; securityPolicy SecurityPolicy_TLS13_1_2_2021_06.
GET /health as a mock integration, plus the /app root every domain extends.
Gateway responses UNAUTHORIZED → 401 and ACCESS_DENIED → 403 render the authorizer errorMessage.
Caching disabled with a recorded CKV_AWS_120 suppression.

d.role: The internal routing plane: /health, /domains/** and /gateways/**.
facts: Resource policy: one Deny for AnyPrincipal when aws:SourceVpce is not the interface endpoint.
No explicit Allow — same-account callers are gated purely by their own IAM policy.
AuthorizationType.IAM on every method by default.
loggingLevel INFO with dataTraceEnabled false, so bodies stay out of execution logs. The public API sets no loggingLevel at all.

d.role: The single deployed stage.
facts: JSON access logs with method, ip, protocol, requestTime, resourcePath, responseLength, status, user and caller.
Its access log group retains for one year.

d.role: The single deployed stage.
facts: dataTraceEnabled is false — this is what keeps internal request and response bodies out of logs.

d.role: Account-level CloudWatch role so API Gateway can write access logs.
facts: Uses the managed AmazonAPIGatewayPushToCloudWatchLogs service role policy.
Account-scoped, so it belongs to the core stack rather than a per-stage one.

d.role: One per domain stack that has public routes.
facts: identitySource is the Authorization header.
All of them point at the same shared authorizer function.
local-council never gets one — it has no public routes.

d.role: Everything under /app/{domain}/{version}/…
facts: dvla 7 · udp 6 · uns 4 · groups 2 · example 11 · local-council 0.
Counted as one method per route; the intermediate path Resources are shared and not counted here.
:param segments become {param}.

d.role: Everything under /domains/{domain}/{version}/…
facts: dvla 1 · udp 2 · local-council 2 · example 2.
Each carries a recorded CKV_AWS_59 suppression — access is controlled by the VPC endpoint and the resource policy.

d.role: One catch-all method per service gateway.
facts: Four methods stand in for 28 upstream operations (dvla 10 · udp 10 · uns 6 · travel 2), because routing happens inside each gateway rather than in API Gateway. Travel is development and staging only, so production has three.

d.role: Forces a new deployment once domain stacks have added their resources. Deploy machinery — see it in Delivery.
facts: Depends on every deployed domain stack.
The sorted METHOD:path list is SHA-256 hashed into the deployment description, so it re-runs only when routes change.
A 6-second pause separates the two deployments because createDeployment is rate-limited.

d.role: The single public entry point for the API.
facts: Two behaviours: the default API behaviour and /docs*.
publishAdditionalMetrics is on — required for the TotalErrorRate alarm, and billed extra.
Logical ID pinned with overrideLogicalId to preserve identity across refactors.
Alias is the zone apex for persistent environments and {stage}.{zone} for ephemeral and personal stages.

d.role: Security headers for the API and for the docs site.
facts: Both: HSTS 365 days with includeSubdomains, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies none.
API only: Content-Security-Policy default-src 'self' and Cache-Control no-store.

d.role: Lets CloudFront read the spec bucket while it stays fully private.
facts: The bucket keeps BlockPublicAccess.BLOCK_ALL.

d.role: Enables the extra CloudFront metrics the alarms need.
facts: Logical ID pinned via overrideLogicalId.

d.role: No custom policies are defined — three managed ones are referenced.
facts: CACHING_DISABLED on the API behaviour, so every request reaches the origin.
CACHING_OPTIMIZED on /docs*.
ALL_VIEWER_EXCEPT_HOST_HEADER as the API origin request policy.

d.role: TLS for the distribution alias.
facts: Must be in us-east-1 for CloudFront.
Validated against the imported hosted zone.

d.role: Points the service name at the distribution.
facts: The hosted zone itself is imported, never created — it belongs to the platform team.
Logical ID pinned via overrideLogicalId.

groups.name: Security · WAF, Shield, IAM, secrets, keys

d.role: Edge filtering.
facts: 0 CommonRuleSet · 1 KnownBadInputs · 2 BypassForE2ETests (allow) · 3 AmazonIpReputationList · 4 RateLimit block at 2000 per IP.
Data protection: SUBSTITUTION on the authorization header.
The bypass is an allow rule, so it terminates evaluation and skips rules 3 and 4 — but not 0 and 1.

d.role: Origin lock on the public API stage.
facts: 0 KnownBadInputs · 1 RequireOriginSecret, an exact byte match on x-origin-verify.
Default block is what makes the raw execute-api URL unusable.
sampledRequestsEnabled is false on the origin-secret rule, so the value is never sampled into logs.

d.role: DDoS protection on the distribution.
facts: Application-layer automatic response runs in count mode — evaluated and reported, not enforced.
Skipped whenever env is development, so neither the dev environment nor any ephemeral or personal stage gets it.

d.role: A hard ceiling on every role in the stack.
facts: One in the platform stack, plus one per deployed domain stack.
Allow: logs, X-Ray, ENI lifecycle, Secrets Manager read, SSM parameter operations, kms:Decrypt, sts:AssumeRole.
Allow: execute-api:Invoke restricted to the private API only.
Deny: lambda:InvokeFunction on everything — this is what forces traffic through the API.
Wildcards are intentional, with recorded CKV_AWS_107/108/111 suppressions.

d.role: Execution identities.
facts: One generated execution role per Lambda, all under the permissions boundary.

Hand-written roles: the API Gateway CloudWatch role (auto-named — 'ApiGatewayCloudWatchRole' is only a construct id) and the smoke-test role, the only one with an explicit physical name {env}-flex-smoke-test-role.
Also created by CDK: the Chatbot role, custom-resource roles and the BucketDeployment handler role.
Per-route inline policies come from grantRouteResources and grantRoutePermissions.

d.role: Origin verification and the E2E WAF bypass.
facts: /{stage}/flex-secret/origin-verify-secret — created in eu-west-2, replicated to us-east-1.
/{stage}/flex-secret/waf/e2e-bypass — created in us-east-1, replicated to eu-west-2.
Both use AWS managed keys, with a recorded CKV_AWS_149 suppression so replication stays simple.
Consumer configs and hash secrets are imported, not created here.

d.role: Encrypts the flow-log bucket.
facts: The only statement the stack adds is the write path for delivery.logs.amazonaws.com — Encrypt, GenerateDataKey* and DescribeKey, conditioned on source account and source ARN. CDK's default account-root statement is also present.

No reader grant is written on top of CDK's default account-root kms:* statement, so decrypt is delegated to IAM rather than blocked outright — an investigator or Athena role still has to be granted it deliberately.

d.role: Encrypts the eu-west-2 alarm and release topics.
facts: cloudwatch.amazonaws.com is granted encrypt and decrypt.

d.role: Encrypts the us-east-1 relay topics.
facts: Per stage, so every ephemeral and personal stage creates its own.
One key shared by both relay topics — #buildRelay is called twice and handed the same key.
The Chatbot role is granted decrypt on the eu-west-2 key, not this one.

d.role: The fourth key in the system, and the only one FLEX does not create: it protects every Lambda's environment variables.
facts: All three Flex Lambda constructs set environmentEncryption to it and call grantDecrypt on the function, so every route, gateway, authorizer and canary function depends on it.

Its ARN is read from /{env}/flex-param/secret/encryption-key with StringParameter.valueForStringParameter, which bypasses BaseStack.import() and the SsmApp export graph — so unlike every other imported key, a missing or wrong value fails at deploy rather than at synth.
The plain NodejsFunctions (stub JWKS, alarm relays) do not use it — their environments are encrypted with the default AWS managed key.

d.role: Swagger UI plus one OpenAPI 3.1 document per domain.
facts: BlockPublicAccess.BLOCK_ALL; reachable only through CloudFront OAC.
Non-current versions under docs/specs/ expire after 30 days.
RETAIN in persistent environments; DESTROY with autoDeleteObjects for ephemeral and personal stages.
Deployed with prune: false, so specs for domains no longer generated are not deleted. The generator always emits all domains' specs regardless of the deploy target.

d.role: CloudFront standard access logs.
facts: Object Lock GOVERNANCE for 90 days; objects and non-current versions expire at 90 days.
Recorded CKV_AWS_18 suppression — a log bucket does not log itself.

d.role: S3 server access logs for the spec bucket.
facts: Object Lock GOVERNANCE for 365 days.

d.role: Destination for VPC flow logs.
facts: Object Lock GOVERNANCE for 365 days, with lifecycle expiry to match.
Encrypted with the dedicated flow-log key rather than an AWS managed one.

d.role: Denies non-TLS requests on every bucket in the app.
facts: EnforceS3Https visits every Bucket and adds a Deny on s3:* for AnyPrincipal when aws:SecureTransport is false.
Applied at App level, so a new bucket cannot be added without it.

d.role: flex-alerts-critical and flex-alerts-warning.
facts: Every alarm routes to exactly one of these two — except the smoke-test alarm, which has no action attached at all.
cloudwatch.amazonaws.com is granted publish on both.

d.role: Carries formatted release notes from the pipeline.
facts: Only in the development environment, because a release happens once per pipeline run.
The staging and production notify jobs assume the development role to publish here.

d.role: Cross-region alarm forwarding.
facts: Encrypted with alias/{stage}-flex-alerts-relay-key.
The topics and subscriptions are correct; the subscribed Lambdas are not — see the relay functions above.

d.role: flex-alerts-{stage}, plus one flex-releases-{stage}-{channel} per release channel in development.
facts: The count shown is the alerts channel only — development adds one more per configured release channel ID, read at synth time via valueFromLookup.
Guardrail policy ReadOnlyAccess caps what anyone can do from Slack.
Its role is granted kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey on the alarm topic key.

d.role: Triggers the canary.
facts: The only scheduled resource in the system.

groups.name: Observability · CloudWatch, X-Ray
groups.note: Retention is set per destination, never globally — the table below is the whole picture for everything that writes a log. VPC flow logs are the one source covered on the Network tab instead, because where they are written is a network fact.

rows: Object Lock GOVERNANCE 90 days; objects and non-current versions expire to match
S3 server access logging, same construct with the default retention
An explicit log group per API, JSON standard fields — both the public and the private API
Auto-created group, no retention configured. Private API only — the public stage sets no loggingLevel
Every function built on the Flex* constructs; the stub JWKS, alarm-relay and BucketDeployment Lambdas use auto-created groups with no expiry

d.role: Error rate, throttles and duration.
facts: Error rate: IF(invocations ≥ 10, 100*(errors/invocations), 0) above 1% for two consecutive 5-minute periods → critical.
Throttles: any throttle in a 1-minute window → critical.
Duration: p99 above 80% of the function's configured timeout over 5 minutes → warning.
Covers domain routes, service gateways and the authorizer. The canary opts out; the relay and stub JWKS functions never had them.
The construct throws at synth if a function has no explicit timeout.

d.role: Error rates and latency.
facts: 5XX average above 1% over five consecutive 1-minute periods → critical.
4XX average above 5% on the same schedule → warning.
End-to-end p95 latency above 3000 ms, 2 of 3 consecutive 5-minute periods → warning.
Integration p95 latency above 2900 ms on the same schedule → warning.
Both latency alarms are gated at 40 requests per period, so quiet stages stay silent.

d.role: Distribution error rates.
facts: 5xxErrorRate above 1% over five consecutive minutes → critical.
4xxErrorRate and TotalErrorRate above 5% on the same schedule → warning.
These metrics are already percentages, so the thresholds are 1 and 5, not 0.01 and 0.05.
Must be created in us-east-1 — CloudFront emits metrics only there.

d.role: Edge function health.
facts: Execution errors over five consecutive minutes → critical.
Throttles over five consecutive minutes → critical.
Validation errors over two consecutive minutes → warning.

d.role: Blocking behaviour.
facts: Any managed-rule block in a 5-minute window → critical.
Block rate above 90% of all requests → critical.
Anomaly detection at 2 standard deviations on blocked volume, 2 of 3 periods → warning.
CLOUDFRONT-scope metrics carry no Region dimension; REGIONAL ones do.

d.role: DDoS signals.
facts: DDoSDetected maximum above 0 in a 1-minute period → critical.
DDoSAttackRequestsPerSecond above 0 → warning.
Created only alongside the Shield protection, so development and every ephemeral stage have neither.
Both logical IDs are pinned via overrideLogicalId.

d.role: No successful canary run in 15 minutes.
facts: It notifies nobody. {stage}-smoke-test-no-success is the one Alarm in the app with no addAlarmAction — actionsEnabled is true, but no topic is attached.
treatMissingData is BREACHING, so a canary that stops running entirely still alarms — into the void.
Metric Flex/SmokeTest.SmokeTestSuccess, summed over a 15-minute period.

d.role: One per Flex Lambda construct, plus one per API stage.
facts: Created explicitly rather than left to Lambda's implicit default, so retention is guaranteed. The count excludes the auto-created groups in the table above.
Content is redacted at source by the @flex/logging sanitizer before it is ever written.
FlexLogger.setLogLevel returns without doing anything when FLEX_ENVIRONMENT is production, so verbose logging cannot be turned on there at runtime.

d.role: Active on every Flex Lambda construct and both API stages.
facts: xray:PutTraceSegments and PutTelemetryRecords sit in the permissions boundary baseline.
Nothing in the us-east-1 global stack is traced, and the plain NodejsFunctions (stub JWKS, alarm relays) are not either.
Segments are emitted by the Lambda execution environment, not through a VPC endpoint — there is no X-Ray interface endpoint.

d.role: Replaces CloudFormation exports for all cross-stack wiring.
facts: Core writes 14: nine VPC parameters plus two security groups, two alarm topics and the API Gateway endpoint. Development adds the release topic (15).
exportVpc is the reason the VPC contributes nine: id, CIDR, AZs, and subnet-id plus route-table-id lists for each of the three tiers.
Platform writes 8: three public API keys, four private API keys and the origin-verify secret ARN.
An ephemeral or personal stage writes only the platform 8 — it imports the rest from development.
SsmApp records the owning stack per (region, key) and throws on duplicate ownership.

d.role: Values owned by flex-params and the platform team.
facts: /infra/dns/hostedzoneid and hostedzonename.
/{env}/flex-param/auth/* — user pool and client IDs, plus stub equivalents.
/{env}/flex-param/monitoring/* — Slack workspace and channel IDs, plus the release channel list in development.
/{env}/flex-param/{gateway}/* — derived from each gateway config's resources rather than hard-coded.

/{env}/flex-param/secret/encryption-key — the Lambda environment CMK ARN. It is the one exception to the rule below: resolveEncryptionKey reads it with valueForStringParameter, outside the export graph, so it is never checked at synth.
Everything else is declared as an external export, so an unknown key fails at synth rather than at deploy.

d.role: Lets the us-east-1 stack read eu-west-2 parameters.
facts: Seven distinct keys are read this way in every stage — the hosted zone id and name, the public REST API id and its app root, the origin-verify secret ARN, and both alarm topic ARNs. Reads are cached per key, so that is seven custom resources.
The physical resource ID embeds a timestamp, so the value is re-read on every update.
Domain kms, secret and ssm resources do not go through this path at all — they are looked up directly and bypass the SsmApp dependency graph by design.

d.role: Scheduled sensitive-data discovery over the CloudFront access-log bucket.
facts: Fully implemented, but its import and its instantiation are commented out in app.ts — it is disabled in code, not merely undeployed. Uncommenting is not a one-line change: the commented block also references a globalStack variable that no longer exists.
The session is enabled through a macie2:enableMacie call with FIFTEEN_MINUTES finding publication; automated discovery explicitly disabled to avoid rolling scans of public specs and log buckets.
A weekly SCHEDULED job every Monday at 100% sampling with RECOMMENDED managed identifiers.
Results export to a KMS-encrypted RETAIN bucket under macie-results/.

The CI coverage check is live: validate:macie-coverage runs in the Hygiene job on every pull request and posts a Slack notice for uncovered domains — so coverage is reported against a stack that is not deployed.
